q.s: The Harappan site of Rakhigarhi, one of the largest sites of the civilisation, is located in which district of Haryana?
q.x: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar district; Banawali is in Fatehabad and Bhagwanpura in Kurukshetra.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Haryana?
q.x: Kalibangan is in Hanumangarh district of Rajasthan; the other three are in Haryana.

q.s: The Harappan site of Kalibangan in Rajasthan was first excavated in 1953 by:
q.x: A. Ghosh discovered Kalibangan (1953); B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar excavated it later. Y. D. Sharma excavated Ropar and J. P. Joshi Surkotada.

q.s: The Harappan site of Surkotada in Kutch, Gujarat, was excavated in 1964 by:
q.x: J. P. Joshi excavated Surkotada in 1964; S. R. Rao excavated Lothal.

q.s: Unlike Mohenjodaro, which was built of burnt brick, the Harappan city of Dholavira was built mainly of:
q.x: Dholavira in Kutch was built mainly of stone; mud brick is notable at Kalibangan.

q.s: The standard ratio of Harappan bricks (thickness : width : length) was:
q.x: Harappan bricks followed the standard ratio 1:2:4.

q.s: Which of the following statements about animals in the Indus Valley Civilisation is correct?
o: Horse bones are well established in the early and mature levels
The water buffalo was the favoured domestic animal
Camel bones have been found only at Lothal
Copper figures of a rhinoceros and an elephant come from Daimabad
q.x: Daimabad yielded these copper figures; camel bones come from Kalibangan and the humped bull was the favoured animal.

q.s: Which animal was the favoured domestic animal of the Harappans, frequently depicted on their seals?
q.x: The humped bull (zebu) was the favoured animal; horse remains are not well established in mature levels.

q.s: The chief port of the Harappan Civilisation, known for its dockyard, was:
q.x: Lothal in Gujarat was the chief port with a dockyard; Harappa was an inland city on the Ravi.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites was NOT a coastal settlement?
q.x: Kalibangan lies inland on the Ghaggar in Rajasthan; the others were coastal sites.

q.s: A painted jar from which Harappan site depicts the story of the cunning fox, similar to a Panchatantra tale?
q.x: A painted jar from Lothal shows the crow and the cunning fox story.

q.s: Recent scientific dating has made which site in Tamil Nadu the source of the oldest known iron in India?
q.x: Iron from Sivagalai in Thoothukudi district has been dated to the early 3rd millennium BCE, the oldest so far.

q.s: Adichanallur, a well-known Iron Age urn-burial site of South India, is located in which district?
q.x: Adichanallur is in Thoothukudi district; Mayiladumparai is in Krishnagiri.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, the king's share of the produce, usually one-sixth, was called:
q.x: Bhaga was the king's share of the produce, generally one-sixth; Shulka meant customs or tolls.

q.s: In the Later Vedic period, the main burden of paying taxes and tribute fell on the:
q.x: The Vaishyas were the chief tribute-payers; Brahmanas and Kshatriyas were exempt.

q.s: According to the Aitareya Brahmana, the ruler of the eastern region was given the title of:
q.x: East – Samrat; South – Bhoja; West – Svarat; North – Virat.

q.s: Which of the following schools of Indian philosophy is classed as nastika because it rejects the authority of the Vedas?
q.x: Charvaka rejects the Vedas and is nastika; Nyaya, Mimamsa and Sankhya are astika schools.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the six orthodox (astika) schools of Indian philosophy?
q.x: Buddhism, like Jainism and Charvaka, rejects the Vedas and is nastika.

q.s: At the First Buddhist Council, the Vinaya Pitaka was recited by:
q.x: Upali recited the Vinaya and Ananda the Sutta; Mahakassapa presided.

q.s: The two merchants who became the first lay disciples of the Buddha were:
q.x: Tapassu and Bhallika offered food to the Buddha after enlightenment and became his first lay disciples.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a cause of the decline of Buddhism in India?
q.x: Ashoka's patronage spread Buddhism; Sanskrit, Vajrayana ritualism and hostile rulers contributed to its decline.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the stupa is correct?
o: The concept of the stupa is older than Buddhism
The stupa was invented by Ashoka
The word 'stupa' first appears in Buddhist texts
Stupas were built only by the Jains
q.x: The stupa grew out of pre-Buddhist burial mounds and the word occurs in Vedic texts.

q.s: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, attained nirvana at:
q.x: Mahavira attained nirvana at Pavapuri; Neminatha at Girnar and Vasupujya at Champapuri.

q.s: The 22nd Tirthankara Neminatha is believed to have attained nirvana at:
q.x: Neminatha's nirvana is associated with Girnar (Urjayanta) in Gujarat.

q.s: Vardhamana Mahavira was born at:
q.x: Mahavira was born at Kundagrama near Vaishali; Lumbini is the Buddha's birthplace.

q.s: Mahavira's mother Trishala was a princess of which clan?
q.x: Trishala was a Lichchhavi princess, sister of Chetaka; his father Siddhartha headed the Jnatrika clan.

q.s: Which of the five great vows of Jainism was added by Mahavira to the four taught by Parshvanatha?
q.x: Mahavira added Brahmacharya (celibacy) to Parshvanatha's four vows.

q.s: The early Jain canonical texts (Agamas) were written in:
q.x: The Jain Agamas are in Ardhamagadhi; Pali is the language of the Buddhist canon.

q.s: Under the Mauryas, Tosali was the provincial capital of:
q.x: Tosali was the capital of Kalinga; Taxila the north, Ujjain the west and Suvarnagiri the south.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Mauryan provincial capital?
q.x: Taxila, Ujjain, Tosali and Suvarnagiri were provincial capitals; Kanchi was the later Pallava capital.

q.s: The Greek envoy Megasthenes, author of 'Indica', came to the court of:
q.x: Megasthenes was sent by Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya.

q.s: Deimachus came as an envoy of Antiochus I to the court of:
q.x: Deimachus (from Antiochus I) and Dionysius (from Ptolemy II) came to Bindusara's court.

q.s: In the Mauryan judicial system, the Kantakashodhana courts dealt with:
q.x: Kantakashodhana courts tried criminal cases; Dharmasthiya courts tried civil cases.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mauryan judiciary is correct?
o: Dharmasthiya courts tried civil cases and had three dharmasthas
The Pradvivaka was the chief tax collector
Mauryan courts had no appointed judges
q.x: Dharmasthiya courts were civil courts with three dharmasthas; the Pradvivaka was the chief judge.

q.s: Under the Mauryas, which of the following was NOT a state monopoly?
q.x: Mining, salt and liquor were state monopolies; textiles were produced largely by guilds and private artisans.

q.s: During the Gupta age, the term 'Chinansuka' referred to:
q.x: Chinansuka denoted silk cloth imported from China.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a port of western India in the Gupta age?
q.x: Tamralipti was a port of eastern India (Bengal); Sopara, Cambay and Broach were western ports.

q.s: Harshavardhana was defeated on the banks of the Narmada by:
q.x: The Chalukya king Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada, as recorded in the Aihole inscription.

q.s: The Aihole inscription, which records Pulakesin II's victory over Harsha, was composed by:
q.x: Ravikirti, the court poet of Pulakesin II, composed the Aihole inscription (634 CE).

q.s: The Virupaksha temple, built by Lokamahadevi, queen of Vikramaditya II, to commemorate his victory over the Pallavas, is at:
q.x: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was modelled on the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi.

q.s: The Maldive islands were conquered by which Chola ruler?
q.x: Rajaraja I conquered the Maldives and destroyed the Chera navy at Kandalur Salai.

q.s: The Sinhalese ruler who drove the Cholas out of Sri Lanka around 1070 CE was:
q.x: Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas around 1070 CE; Mahinda V had been captured by Rajendra I.

q.s: According to the Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I, the age limit for candidates to village committees was:
q.x: Candidates had to be between 35 and 70, own one-fourth veli of tax-paying land and a house on their own site.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a qualification for candidates to village committees under the Uttaramerur inscriptions?
o: Ownership of one-fourth veli of tax-paying land
Ownership of a house on one's own site
Knowledge of Vedic mantras and Brahmanas
q.x: The rules required tax-paying land, a house, age 35-70 and Vedic learning; guild membership was not a condition.

q.s: The irrigation cess 'haq-i-sharb' was introduced by:
q.x: Firoz Shah Tughlaq levied haq-i-sharb, one-tenth of the produce, on canal-irrigated land.

q.s: Firoz Shah Tughlaq's longest canal, about 150 miles long, brought water from the Yamuna to:
q.x: His 150-mile canal ran from the Yamuna to Hisar; the Rajabwah was later restored under Akbar as the Shihab canal.

q.s: The last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate, defeated at the First Battle of Panipat (1526), was:
q.x: Ibrahim Lodi was defeated and killed by Babur at Panipat in 1526.

q.s: Who was the last ruler of the Khalji dynasty?
q.x: Qutbuddin Mubarak Shah, killed by Khusrau Khan in 1320, was the last Khalji; Kaiqubad was the last Slave ruler.

q.s: The 'Rumi method' (araba) used by Babur at Panipat involved:
o: Chaining carts together as a barrier for gunners
q.x: Carts were tied together as a shield for matchlockmen and guns, combined with the tulughma flanking tactic.

q.s: Which of the following battles was NOT fought by Babur?
q.x: Chausa (1539) was fought between Humayun and Sher Shah; Babur died in 1530.

q.s: Under Sher Shah Suri, the officer responsible for law and order in a sarkar was the:
q.x: The Chief Shiqdar kept law and order; the Chief Munsif handled revenue and civil matters; the Fotedar was the treasurer.

q.s: In the Mughal mansabdari system, the 'sawar' rank indicated:
o: The number of cavalrymen to be maintained
The personal rank and salary of the officer
q.x: Sawar denoted the cavalry a mansabdar had to maintain; zat denoted personal rank and pay.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mughal mansabdari system is correct?
o: The zat rank denoted the number of cavalrymen
Umara were mansabdars holding 1,000 sawar or above
For every 10 sawars a mansabdar had to keep 20 horses
q.x: The rule was 20 horses per 10 sawars; umara held 1,000 zat or above, and mansabs were not hereditary.

q.s: In which year was the Red Fort Complex, Delhi, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
q.x: The Red Fort Complex was inscribed in 2007; Agra Fort in 1983, Fatehpur Sikri in 1986 and Humayun's Tomb in 1993.

q.s: Which of the following Mughal monuments is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
q.x: Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad is not inscribed; the other three are World Heritage Sites.

q.s: The Bhakti saint Kabir was a disciple of:
q.x: Kabir, raised by the weaver couple Niru and Nima, was a disciple of Ramananda.

q.s: Rejecting the belief that death at Kashi assured liberation, Kabir chose to die at:
q.x: Kabir chose to die at Maghar, which was believed to bring rebirth as a donkey, to challenge the Kashi belief.

q.s: Basavanna, the founder of the Virashaiva (Lingayat) movement, was a minister of which ruler?
q.x: Basavanna was minister of the Kalachuri king Bijjala II at Kalyana, where he set up the Anubhava Mantapa.

q.s: In Virashaivism, the principle of 'Kayaka' stands for:
q.x: Kayaka means honest work as worship; Dasoha means sharing with others.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Bhakti and Sufi movements is correct?
o: They put an end to the purdah system
Kabir and Nanak criticised the orthodoxy of both Hinduism and Islam
Their traditions never developed into separate sects
q.x: Kabir and Nanak attacked orthodoxy in both faiths; caste and purdah persisted and their followers later formed panths.

q.s: The Naqshbandi Sufi order was introduced in India by:
q.x: Khwaja Baqi Billah brought the Naqshbandi order; Sirhindi was his disciple who opposed Akbar's policies.

q.s: Which Sufi order in India opposed sama (musical assembly) and Akbar's policy of Sulh-i-kul?
q.x: The orthodox Naqshbandis opposed sama and Sulh-i-kul; the Chishtis were fond of sama.

q.s: In Sufism, the hospice where a pir lived with his disciples and which fed travellers and the poor was called:
q.x: The khanqah was the Sufi hospice; a dargah is the shrine at a saint's tomb.

q.s: The Sufi musical assembly meant to produce spiritual ecstasy was known as:
q.x: Sama was the musical assembly; raqs was dance, zikr the repeated remembrance of God.

q.s: The overall commander of the Maratha army at the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was:
q.x: Sadashiv Rao Bhau commanded, with Vishwas Rao as nominal head; both were killed.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT an ally of Ahmad Shah Abdali in the Third Battle of Panipat?
q.x: Suraj Mal of Bharatpur kept away from the battle; the Rohilla Najib-ud-Daula and Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh sided with Abdali.

q.s: In the Battle of Colachel (1741), the Dutch were defeated by:
q.x: Marthanda Varma defeated the Dutch under De Lannoy at Colachel; Forde defeated them at Bedara (1759).

q.s: The Dutch fort called Fort Geldria (1613) stood at:
q.x: Fort Geldria was at Pulicat, the Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel coast; Fort Gustavus was at Chinsura.

q.s: Under Oliver Cromwell's charter of 1657, the English East India Company became:
q.x: Cromwell's 1657 charter put the Company on a permanent joint-stock basis.

q.s: The rival English companies were merged to form the 'United Company of Merchants of England Trading to the East Indies' in:
q.x: The merger was completed in 1708 under the Godolphin award.

q.s: The first Dutch factory on the east coast of India was set up in 1605 at:
q.x: Machilipatnam (1605) was the first; Nizampatnam (1606) the second; Palakollu dates from 1613.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Dutch settlement in Andhra?
q.x: Yanam was a French settlement; the Dutch held Nizampatnam, Palakollu and Bheemunipatnam.

q.s: The book 'India Wins Freedom' was written by:
q.x: 'India Wins Freedom' is Maulana Azad's memoir; 'A Nation in Making' is by S.N. Banerjee.

q.s: 'A Nation in Making' is the autobiography of:
q.x: Surendranath Banerjee wrote 'A Nation in Making' (1925).

q.s: The Treaty of Pondicherry (1754-55), which ended the Second Carnatic War, was signed on the French side by:
q.x: Godeheu, who replaced Dupleix, signed it with Thomas Saunders; Muhammad Ali was recognised as Nawab.

q.s: The birth anniversary of Birsa Munda, 15 November, is observed in India as:
q.x: Since 2021, 15 November is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

q.s: Birsa Munda died in 1900 in the jail at:
q.x: Birsa was captured in Jamkopai forest and died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900.

q.s: The Kuki rising of 1917-19 took place in:
q.x: The Kuki rising was in Manipur; the Khond rising in the Ghumsar hills of Odisha.

q.s: The Bhil risings that began in 1817-19 took place mainly in:
q.x: The Bhils rose in Khandesh in the Western Ghats region.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
q.x: Attlee was the Prime Minister who sent the Mission; its members were Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and Alexander.

q.s: The August Offer (1940) was made during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Linlithgow made the August Offer in 1940; 'The Viceroy's Journal' is by Wavell.

q.s: Under the Ryotwari settlement, the revenue settlement was made directly with the:
q.x: Ryotwari, introduced in Madras and Bombay, dealt directly with the ryot, with periodic revision about every 30 years.

q.s: The Ryotwari system was NOT introduced in which of the following regions?
q.x: Bengal had the Permanent Settlement (1793); Ryotwari was introduced in Madras, Bombay and parts of Assam.

q.s: Noble College, one of the earliest colleges in Andhra, is located at:
q.x: Noble College is at Machilipatnam; the Hindu College at Visakhapatnam is now Mrs A.V.N. College.

q.s: The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up in 1688 at:
q.x: Madras got the first Municipal Corporation in 1688.

q.s: Local self-government became a provincial subject under:
q.x: Local self-government was a transferred provincial subject under the 1919 Act (dyarchy).

q.s: The first Telugu political weekly 'Andhra Prakasika' (1885) was founded by:
q.x: A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu founded Andhra Prakasika in 1885.

q.s: Kandukuri Veeresalingam's journal, through which he campaigned for social reform, was:
q.x: Veeresalingam founded Vivekavardhini (1874); Satya Doota (1835) was the first Telugu journal.

q.s: The book 'Gulamgiri' (1873) was written by:
q.x: Gulamgiri is by Jyotiba Phule; Ambedkar wrote 'The Untouchables' and 'Annihilation of Caste'.

q.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's PhD thesis at Columbia University was titled:
o: The Evolution of Provincial Finance in British India
q.x: His Columbia PhD thesis was 'The Evolution of Provincial Finance in British India'.

q.s: In 'Annihilation of Caste', Ambedkar described caste not merely as a division of labour but as a division of:
q.x: Ambedkar called caste a division of labourers and saw inter-caste marriage as the real remedy.

q.s: During Gandhi's 'Great Trial' of 1922 at Ahmedabad, he was sentenced to six years' imprisonment by Judge:
q.x: Judge C.N. Broomfield sentenced him to six years for his Young India articles; Gandhi pleaded guilty.

q.s: When the Civil Disobedience Movement was resumed, Gandhi was arrested on 4 January 1932 under Viceroy:
q.x: Willingdon succeeded Irwin in 1931 and followed a policy of repression.

q.s: The Civil Disobedience Movement was formally withdrawn by the Congress in:
q.x: After mass satyagraha was suspended in 1933, the CDM was formally withdrawn in April 1934.

q.s: Who was the president of the Naval Central Strike Committee during the Royal Indian Navy revolt of 1946?
q.x: M.S. Khan was president; B.C. Dutt was a rating of HMIS Talwar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Royal Indian Navy revolt of 1946 is correct?
o: The ratings demanded the withdrawal of Indian troops from Indonesia
B.C. Dutt was the president of the Naval Central Strike Committee
It had the official support of the Congress leadership
q.x: The ratings demanded equal pay, release of INA prisoners and withdrawal from Indonesia; the revolt spread to Karachi, Calcutta and other ports.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam, who left the Congress in 1951, formed which party along with N.G. Ranga?
q.x: Prakasam and Ranga formed the Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party in 1951.

q.s: Tanguturi Prakasam gave up his lucrative law practice in 1921 to join the:
q.x: He gave up his practice in 1921 for the Non-Cooperation Movement.

q.s: Gandhi first used satyagraha in South Africa in 1906 against the:
q.x: The 1906 satyagraha in the Transvaal was against the Asiatic Registration Ordinance, the 'Black Act'.

q.s: During the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra, which centre was called the 'Dakshina Dandi'?
q.x: Devarampadu near Ongole was the 'Dakshina Dandi'; Seethanagaram Ashram was the 'Andhra Dandi'.

q.s: The Salt Satyagraha at Mattapalem in Andhra was led by:
q.x: Dandu Narayana Raju led it at Mattapalem; Pattabhi Sitaramayya was associated with Machilipatnam.

q.s: Rashtriya Ekta Diwas (National Unity Day) is observed every year on:
q.x: It marks Sardar Patel's birth anniversary on 31 October.

q.s: The Statue of Unity, the 182 m statue of Sardar Patel, stands on Sadhu Bet island on the river:
q.x: It is near the Sardar Sarovar Dam on the Narmada, Gujarat, inaugurated on 31 October 2018.

q.s: Who was the temporary Chairman of the Constituent Assembly at its first meeting on 9 December 1946?
q.x: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was temporary Chairman; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December.

q.s: The Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights and Minorities of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
q.x: Patel chaired the Advisory Committee; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

q.s: After 1947, Nehru promised a committee on the Andhra demand during his 1948 visit to:
q.x: Nehru made this promise at Visakhapatnam; Andhra had been left out of the Draft Constitution of February 1948.

q.s: The separate Andhra Congress circle (Andhra Provincial Congress Committee) was sanctioned by the Indian National Congress in:
q.x: Despite earlier rebuffs at Madras (1914) and Lucknow (1916), the Congress approved a separate Andhra circle in 1917.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953)?
q.x: The SRC consisted of Fazl Ali (Chairman), H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the States Reorganisation Commission's view on Telangana is correct?
o: It recommended the immediate merger of Telangana with Andhra
It recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Bombay
It allowed merger by a simple majority at any time
It allowed merger after the 1961 elections if two-thirds of the Telangana legislature agreed
q.x: Para 386 required a two-thirds majority after 1961; Raichur and Gulbarga were to go to Mysore.

q.s: Which of the following Chalcolithic cultures of India began the earliest?
q.x: Ahar-Banas began the earliest; it and Kayatha were contemporaries of the Harappans, and Jorwe was the latest.

q.s: The Nasik inscription, which describes the achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni, was issued by his mother:
q.x: Gautami Balasri issued the Nasik prasasti in the reign of her grandson Vasishthiputra Pulumavi.

q.s: The Naneghat inscription, recording Vedic sacrifices performed by the early Satavahanas, was issued by Queen:
q.x: Naganika, queen of Satakarni I, issued the Naneghat inscription.

q.s: Dhanyakataka, a capital of the later Satavahanas, is identified with:
q.x: Dhanyakataka is Amaravati–Dharanikota on the Krishna.

q.s: The stupa excavated at Vaddamanu in Guntur district belongs to which religion?
q.x: The Vaddamanu stupa is a Jain stupa, a rare example in Andhra.

q.s: In Satavahana administration, an 'Ahara' (district) was headed by an:
q.x: An Amatya, often a relative of the king, headed an Ahara; distant aharas were under Mahasenadhipatis.

q.s: The oldest stupa in Andhra Pradesh, whose relic caskets mention Raja Kubiraka, is at:
q.x: Bhattiprolu, excavated by Alexander Rea in 1892, is the oldest stupa in AP.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Buddhist stupa site of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Lepakshi is a Vijayanagara-era Veerabhadra temple; the others are stupa sites.

q.s: Who called Amaravati art the 'epitome of Indian architecture' and wrote 'Tree and Serpent Worship'?
q.x: James Fergusson wrote 'Tree and Serpent Worship' (1868).

q.s: A large part of the Amaravati stupa sculptures is now kept in the:
q.x: Most Amaravati sculptures are in the British Museum and the Government Museum, Chennai.

q.s: Adavi Santisri, daughter of the Ikshvaku king Santamula, was married to Skanda Visakha of which family?
q.x: Adavi Santisri married Skanda Visakha of the Dhanikas; Santamula's sister Santisri married into the Pugiyas.

q.s: The Chikkulla plates of the Vishnukundin king Vikramendra Varma II are notable for containing:
o: The earliest Telugu phrase in a royal grant
The first Sanskrit kavya in Andhra
A grant to a Jain vihara
q.x: They contain the Telugu phrase 'Vijaya rajya samvatsarambul'; the Polamuru plates describe divine ordeals.

q.s: The Velpuru pillar inscription is associated with which Vishnukundin ruler?
q.x: The Velpuru pillar belongs to Madhava Varma II; Ramatirtham to Indravarma.

q.s: The Undavalli caves near Vijayawada are famous for a monolithic image of:
q.x: The centrepiece is the reclining Vishnu; the four-storeyed caves were cut top-down.

q.s: Which of the following rock-cut cave temples is NOT located in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Ellora is in Maharashtra; the other three are in Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: Kirtivarman II, the last ruler of the Badami Chalukyas, was overthrown by the Rashtrakuta king:
q.x: Dantidurga founded Rashtrakuta power by overthrowing Kirtivarman II around 753 CE.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the later Badami Chalukyas is correct?
o: Vikramaditya II left a Tamil inscription at Kanchi
Vikramaditya II took Kanchi but spared the city
Lokamahadevi built the Virupaksha temple at Aihole
Kirtivarman II was overthrown by the Rashtrakuta Dhruva
q.x: He spared Kanchi and left a Kannada inscription there; the Virupaksha temple is at Pattadakal and Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II.

q.s: 'Parasara Madhaveeyam', the main law book of the Vijayanagara kingdom, is a commentary on the:
q.x: Madhavacharya's work comments on the Parashara Smriti; the Mitakshara comments on the Yajnavalkya Smriti.

q.s: The founder of the Reddi kingdom (1324-25), who expelled Tughlaq forces from coastal Andhra, was:
q.x: Prolaya Vema Reddi founded the kingdom with Addanki as his capital.

q.s: 'Srungara Deepika', a commentary on the Amaru Shataka, was written by the Reddi king:
q.x: Pedakomati Vema wrote Srungara Deepika and Saptasati Saratika; Kataya Vema wrote Kumaragiri Rajiyam.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by a Reddi king?
q.x: Kavyalankara Chudamani is by the poet Vinnakota Peddana; the others are by Pedakomati Vema and Kataya Vema.

q.s: Before the creation of districts in 1794, the Northern Circars were administered by Chiefs and Councils at Machilipatnam and:
q.x: The Circars were run by Chiefs and Councils at Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam until 1794.

q.s: The Carnatic districts of Nellore and Chittoor came under British control by a treaty (1801) with Nawab:
q.x: The 1801 treaty with Azim-ud-Daula transferred the Carnatic to the Company.

q.s: The West Godavari district was formed in:
q.x: West Godavari was formed in 1925; Guntur and East Godavari in 1904, Chittoor in 1911.

q.s: Anantapur district was carved out of Bellary district in:
q.x: Anantapur was formed in 1882; Kurnool district dates from 1858.

q.s: The Palnadu forest satyagraha of 1921-22 was led by:
q.x: Kanneganti Hanumanthu led it in Palnadu (Guntur district) during Non-Cooperation.

q.s: Madduri Annapurnayya, known as 'Andhra Netaji', was the first Andhra leader to join:
q.x: He led the Andhra branch of the Forward Bloc and was jailed for the playlet 'Chichula Pidugu'.

q.s: The Telangana Armed Struggle was sparked by the killing of Doddi Komaraiah in 1946 at:
q.x: Doddi Komaraiah was killed at Kadavendi (Jangaon) in July 1946; the struggle lasted till 1951.

q.s: The Munagala paragana peasant struggle took place in a zamindari then part of which district?
q.x: Munagala was then in Nandigama taluk of Krishna district.

q.s: Which of the following statements about drama troupes (Nataka Samasthalu) in the freedom movement is correct?
o: They could carry political ideas to large illiterate audiences
They were patronised by the colonial government
They performed only mythological plays with no political content
They were banned by the Congress
q.x: As the main mass entertainment, troupes spread nationalist ideas to thousands at once, so officials watched them closely.

q.s: The Sribagh Pact (16 November 1937) was signed at the Madras residence of:
q.x: Sribagh was Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house in Madras.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the 'Granthalayodyama Trimurthulu' of the Andhra library movement?
q.x: The three were Kasinathuni, Ayyanki and Gadicherla; Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited Krishna Patrika.

q.s: The Greyhounds, the elite anti-Naxal force of the Andhra Pradesh Police, was raised in:
q.x: The Greyhounds were raised in 1989; the PWG was banned in 1992.

q.s: Sri Sri's landmark collection of revolutionary poems that broke traditional Telugu prosody is:
q.x: Maha Prasthanam is Sri Sri's work; Gabbilam is by Jashuva.

q.s: Sri Sri was the first president of which literary organisation?
q.x: Sri Sri was the first president of Virasam (1970).

q.s: The Optimum Population Theory is associated with:
q.x: Edwin Cannan is associated with optimum population; Malthus wrote the Essay on the Principle of Population (1798).

q.s: Which of the following statements about population theories is correct?
o: The demographic transition theory was given by Edwin Cannan
Malthus held that food grows faster than population
Malthus held that population grows geometrically while food grows arithmetically
The optimum population theory was given by Malthus
q.x: Malthus (1798) contrasted geometric population growth with arithmetic food growth; Cannan gave optimum population theory.

q.s: The book 'Modernization of Indian Tradition' (1973) was written by:
q.x: Yogendra Singh wrote it, distinguishing orthogenetic (internal) and heterogenetic (external) change.

q.s: Which sociologist described secularisation as the 'disenchantment of the world'?
q.x: Max Weber used the phrase 'disenchantment of the world'.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT generally recognised as a basis of social stratification?
q.x: Stratification ranks groups by unequal wealth, prestige and power; language is not counted as a basis.

q.s: The book 'Imagined Communities' on the origins of nationalism was written by:
q.x: Benedict Anderson wrote 'Imagined Communities'; Barth wrote 'Ethnic Groups and Boundaries'.

q.s: The SNDP Yogam (1903) in Kerala is associated with:
q.x: Sree Narayana Guru inspired the SNDP Yogam; his Aruvippuram consecration was in 1888.

q.s: Periyar E.V. Ramasamy was jailed in 1924 for his part in the satyagraha at:
q.x: Periyar led the Vaikom Satyagraha (1924), earning the title 'Vaikom Veerar'.

q.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A was created by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 89th Amendment (2003) split the joint commission; the NCST came into being in 2004.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the NCSC and NCST is correct?
o: The NCST Chairperson holds the rank of a Minister of State
Each has a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and three members
They present their reports directly to Parliament
Consulting them on major policy matters is optional
q.x: The Chairperson has Cabinet rank, reports go to the President and consultation under Art. 338(9) is mandatory.

q.s: Separate electorates as a cause of communalism in India are best classified as a:
q.x: Separate electorates (1909) were a colonial policy; relative deprivation is an economic cause.

q.s: The committee set up in 2010 to examine the demand for a separate Telangana state was headed by:
q.x: The Srikrishna Committee submitted its report in December 2010.

q.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh receives the lowest average annual rainfall (about 544 mm)?
q.x: Anantapur gets about 544 mm against up to 1,250 mm in north coastal districts.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the literacy rate of Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: AP's literacy (67.35%) was below the national average of about 74%.

q.s: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 gives effect to which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: The RTE Act gives effect to Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment.

q.s: Under the RTE Act, the 25 per cent reservation for disadvantaged children does NOT apply to:
q.x: Minority institutions are exempt from the 25 per cent quota.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh scheme 'YSR Kalyanamasthu' provides:
o: Financial aid for the marriage of poor brides
q.x: YSR Kalyanamasthu gives marriage assistance to poor brides; YSR Aasara covers SHG loans.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act is correct?
o: Section 18A requires a preliminary enquiry before an FIR
A Special Court imposes collective fines on an area
A Special Court may remove a likely offender from a Scheduled area for up to two years
Anticipatory bail is freely available to the accused
q.x: Collective fines are imposed by the State Government; Section 18A removes preliminary enquiry; anticipatory bail is barred.

q.s: The New Prime Minister's 15 Point Programme for the Welfare of Minorities was launched in:
q.x: The original programme dates from 1983 and the new one from 2006, earmarking about 15% of targets in selected schemes.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an objective of the Prime Minister's New 15 Point Programme for minorities?
o: Delinking Scheduled Caste status from religion
Equitable share in economic activities and employment
Prevention and control of communal riots
q.x: Delinking SC status from religion was a Ranganath Misra Commission recommendation.

q.s: The Sachar Committee on the social, economic and educational status of Muslims submitted its report in:
q.x: Set up in March 2005, it reported in November 2006 and proposed an Equal Opportunity Commission.

q.s: The Sachar Committee identified which group as the most deprived section among Indian Muslims?
q.x: It named the Arzal (groups with SC-like status) as the most deprived.

q.s: India ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) in:
q.x: The UNGA adopted the UNCRPD in December 2006 and India ratified it in October 2007; the RPwD Act came into force in 2017.

q.s: The headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) is located at:
q.x: The AIIB is headquartered in Beijing; the New Development Bank is in Shanghai.

q.s: Border trade between India and China through which pass in Sikkim was reopened in 2006?
q.x: Nathu La reopened for border trade in 2006; the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra uses Lipulekh and Nathu La.

q.s: Which country is the second-largest shareholder in the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
q.x: China is the largest shareholder and India the second-largest; the USA and Japan are not members.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
q.x: The USA and Japan are not AIIB members.

q.s: The World Trade Organization, TRIPS and GATS were created as a result of which round of GATT negotiations?
q.x: The Uruguay Round (1986-94) created the WTO; the Kennedy Round produced the first Anti-Dumping Code.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the I2U2 grouping?
q.x: I2U2 consists of India, Israel, the UAE and the USA.

q.s: The G4 nations seeking permanent seats in the UN Security Council are India, Brazil, Japan and:
q.x: The G4 consists of India, Brazil, Germany and Japan.

q.s: Which of the following countries is on the FATF 'black list' along with Iran and North Korea?
q.x: Myanmar, Iran and North Korea are on the black list; Pakistan left the grey list in October 2022.

q.s: India became a full member of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) in:
q.x: India joined FATF in 2010 and is also a member of the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering.

q.s: China's first overseas military base, set up in 2017, is located at:
q.x: China's first overseas base is in Djibouti in the Horn of Africa.

q.s: The UK agreed in a May 2025 treaty to transfer sovereignty over the Chagos Islands, including Diego Garcia, to:
q.x: The UK–Mauritius treaty transferred the Chagos Islands while keeping the Diego Garcia base on lease.

q.s: Dr B.R. Ambedkar was first elected to the Constituent Assembly from:
q.x: He was first elected from Bengal; after Partition he was elected from Bombay in the seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.

q.s: Which of the following Fundamental Rights is available ONLY to citizens of India?
o: Protection of life and personal liberty (Article 21)
q.x: Article 19 freedoms are for citizens only; Articles 14, 21 and 25 apply to all persons.

q.s: Article 23 of the Indian Constitution prohibits:
o: Traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar)
q.x: Article 23 bans trafficking and begar; Article 24 bans child labour in hazardous work.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 23 is correct?
o: The State must pay remuneration in every case of compulsory service
'Begar' means forced labour for which fair wages are paid
It protects citizens and non-citizens, against the State as well as private persons
While imposing compulsory service the State may discriminate on grounds of caste
q.x: Article 23 applies to all persons and to private persons too; begar is unpaid forced labour.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the Gram Sabha has a role under the Forest Rights Act in deciding on mining in the Niyamgiri hills?
q.x: The Orissa Mining Corporation (Niyamgiri, 2013) case left the decision to the Dongria Kondh Gram Sabhas.

q.s: The Samatha judgment (1997) of the Supreme Court relates to:
o: Ban on leasing tribal land in Schedule V areas to non-tribals
q.x: Samatha v. State of AP barred leasing Scheduled Area land to non-tribals and private companies.

q.s: Article 31C of the Constitution was inserted by the:
q.x: The 25th Amendment inserted Article 31C; its extension by the 42nd Amendment was struck down in Minerva Mills (1980).

q.s: The Supreme Court held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights in which case of 1967?
q.x: Golaknath (1967) held FRs unamendable; Kesavananda (1973) replaced it with the basic structure doctrine.

q.s: Under Article 110(3) of the Constitution, the final decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill rests with the:
q.x: The Speaker's decision is final and his certificate is endorsed on the Bill.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution lays down the procedure for the impeachment of the President?
q.x: Article 61 deals with impeachment; Article 53 vests the executive power in the President.

q.s: Which Article makes it the duty of the Prime Minister to keep the President informed of Cabinet decisions?
q.x: Article 78 lays down the duties of the PM towards the President.

q.s: The Cabinet Secretariat of the Government of India functions directly under the:
q.x: The Cabinet Secretariat is under the PM; the Cabinet Secretary heads the civil services.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Cabinet Secretary is correct?
o: He works under the Ministry of Home Affairs
He is appointed by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet
He is first in the Table of Precedence
q.x: The ACC appoints the Cabinet Secretary, who chairs the Civil Services Board and is 11th in the Table of Precedence.

q.s: The parliamentary form of government is also known as 'responsible government' because:
o: The judiciary is responsible to Parliament
The Governor is responsible to the State legislature
The President is responsible to the people
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the lower House
q.x: The executive remains in office only while it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.

q.s: Unlike the USA, in India the residuary powers of legislation are vested in the:
q.x: In India residuary powers are with the Union (Article 248); in the USA they lie with the States.

q.s: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, appeals against orders of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission lie with the:
q.x: Appeals from the National Commission go to the Supreme Court.

q.s: Under the 2021 jurisdiction rules, a District Consumer Commission can hear complaints where the value of goods or services is up to:
q.x: District – up to ₹50 lakh; State – ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore; National – above ₹2 crore.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT part of the divisible pool of central taxes shared with the States?
q.x: Cesses and surcharges are kept out of the divisible pool, so their rise reduces the States' real share.

q.s: The committee that recommends the appointment of the Chairperson of the NHRC is headed by the:
q.x: The six-member committee is headed by the PM; the CJI is not a member.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends the NHRC Chairperson?
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
q.x: The committee has the PM, Speaker, Home Minister, RS Deputy Chairman and both Leaders of Opposition; the CJI is not a member.

q.s: Under the RTI Act, information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be provided within:
q.x: Section 7 requires information within 30 days, or 48 hours where life or liberty is involved.

q.s: Under Section 20 of the RTI Act, the maximum penalty that can be imposed on a Public Information Officer is:
q.x: The penalty is ₹250 per day up to a maximum of ₹25,000.

q.s: Under Section 6(2) of the RTI Act, 2005, an applicant seeking information:
o: Must state the reason for the request
Must be a resident of the State
q.x: Section 6(2) says no reason need be given for seeking information.

q.s: In CBSE v. Aditya Bandopadhyay (2011), the Supreme Court held that under the RTI Act:
o: Asset declarations of officials are public
q.x: The Court held evaluated answer sheets are 'information' that candidates can access.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for elections on the basis of adult suffrage?
q.x: Article 326 provides adult suffrage; Article 324 vests superintendence of elections in the ECI.

q.s: Elections to panchayats in a State are conducted by the:
q.x: Under Articles 243K and 243ZA, State Election Commissions conduct panchayat and municipal polls.

q.s: Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPIC) were introduced in 1993 under Chief Election Commissioner:
q.x: T.N. Seshan introduced EPIC in 1993.

q.s: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, which enabled linking of Aadhaar with electoral rolls, was passed in:
q.x: The 2021 Act enabled voluntary Aadhaar linking and four qualifying dates a year.

q.s: The three-tier Panchayati Raj system in Andhra Pradesh came into force on:
q.x: AP introduced the three-tier system from 1 November 1959, soon after Rajasthan (2 October 1959).

q.s: In 1986 Andhra Pradesh replaced the block-level Panchayat Samithis with:
q.x: The Mandal Praja Parishads Act, 1986 replaced Panchayat Samithis, an idea from the Ashok Mehta Committee.

q.s: The gap between the revenue-raising powers and the spending responsibilities of the Union and the States is called:
q.x: Vertical imbalance arises as the Union holds buoyant taxes while States carry heavier spending duties.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the primary statutory auditor of Panchayat Raj Institutions is the:
q.x: The State Audit Department (renamed under the AP State Audit Act, 1989) audits PRIs; the CAG gives technical guidance and support.

q.s: The proviso to Article 164(1) requires a Minister in charge of tribal welfare in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and:
q.x: The 94th Amendment (2006) replaced Bihar with Chhattisgarh; the four States are Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP and Odisha.

q.s: The Women's Reservation Act (106th Amendment) was passed by Parliament in September 2023 after being introduced as the:
q.x: It was introduced as the 128th Amendment Bill; the 108th Bill had passed the Rajya Sabha in 2010 and lapsed in 2014.

q.s: The first State in India to reserve 50 per cent of panchayat seats for women (2006) was:
q.x: Bihar led in 2006; this is possible because the constitutional one-third is a floor, not a ceiling.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a criticism of India's economic reforms after 1991?
o: Sharp rise in public investment in agriculture
Use of disinvestment proceeds to plug revenue gaps
Undervaluation of PSU assets during disinvestment
q.x: Public investment in agriculture fell after 1991; the other three are standard criticisms.

q.s: Viability Gap Funding (VGF) in India is a grant given to PPP infrastructure projects that are:
q.x: VGF bridges the gap for economically justified but commercially unviable projects; the Centre normally gives up to 20%.

q.s: The Public Private Partnership Appraisal Committee (PPPAC) for central projects is chaired by the:
q.x: PPPAC is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs.

q.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission aims at green hydrogen production capacity of how many million tonnes per annum by 2030?
q.x: The target is 5 MMTA by 2030, with MNRE as nodal ministry.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a green hydrogen hub under the National Green Hydrogen Mission?
q.x: The hubs are Kandla, Paradip and Tuticorin.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three dimensions of the UNDP Human Development Index?
q.x: Voice and accountability is one of the six World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators, not an HDI dimension.

q.s: The Competition Commission of India functions under the administrative control of the:
q.x: The CCI is under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and became fully functional in 2009.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Competition Commission of India is correct?
o: It consists of a Chairperson and 2 to 6 other members
It functions under the Ministry of Finance
The original Competition Act allowed up to 6 members
q.x: The CCI became fully functional in 2009; the original Act allowed up to 10 members.

q.s: According to the Economic Survey 2018-19, India's demographic dividend will peak around:
q.x: The dividend peaks around 2041, when the working-age (20-59) share will be about 59%.

q.s: As per the Census of India, a 'Class I' town is one with a population of:
q.x: Class I towns have 1 lakh or more people; small towns are Class IV-VI.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for a 'Census town'?
o: Presence of a municipality or cantonment board
At least 75% of male main workers in non-agricultural work
Density of at least 400 persons per sq km
q.x: Having a municipality or cantonment makes a statutory town; a census town must meet the other three tests.

q.s: As per Census 2011, the most populous urban agglomeration in India was:
q.x: Greater Mumbai (18.4 million) led, followed by Delhi, Kolkata and Chennai.

q.s: The Anna Canteens reopened in Andhra Pradesh in August 2024 serve meals at a price of:
q.x: Anna Canteens serve meals at ₹5.

q.s: In the NITI Aayog SDG India Index, a State scoring between 65 and 99 is categorised as:
q.x: 65-99 is Front Runner; only 100 is Achiever. AP's score of 74 placed it among Front Runners.

q.s: Foreign exchange reserves of a country are usually assessed in terms of the number of months of:
q.x: Import cover is the standard measure; the Survey cites reserves covering over 11 months of imports.

q.s: The new series of India's national accounts released in February 2026 uses which base year?
q.x: The new series has 2022-23 as its base year, replacing 2011-12.

q.s: Which of the following is a real-sector activity?
q.x: Manufacturing is a real-sector (secondary) activity; banking, shares and insurance belong to the financial sector.

q.s: Per capita income of a State is calculated by dividing which aggregate by its population?
q.x: Per capita income is NSDP divided by population.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh's Gross State Value Added, the sector with the largest share is:
q.x: Services account for the largest share (about 43%), followed by agriculture and allied.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's unorganised sector is correct?
o: It employs less than half of all workers
It employs over 80 per cent of workers
It generates over 80 per cent of output
It provides formal social security to most workers
q.x: The unorganised sector employs over 80% of workers but yields only about 45% of output.

q.s: The capabilities approach to human development is associated with:
q.x: Amartya Sen's capability approach underlies the HDI; Mahbub ul Haq designed the index.

q.s: According to Engel's Law, as family income rises, the share of income spent on food:
q.x: Engel's Law: the food share falls as income rises.

q.s: The UN definition of absolute poverty was adopted at the World Summit for Social Development held in 1995 at:
q.x: The Copenhagen Summit (1995) adopted the definition.

q.s: The first poverty estimate in India based on a calorie norm was made by:
q.x: Dandekar and Rath (1971) first used calories (2,250 per day); Naoroji's estimate was based on subsistence costs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the New Industrial Policy, 1991 is correct?
o: Industries reserved for the public sector were cut from 17 to 8
Compulsory licensing was extended to more industries
Foreign equity was limited to 26 per cent
q.x: MRTP asset limits were scrapped, licensing was abolished for most industries and 51% foreign equity was allowed automatically.

q.s: The term 'jobless growth' refers to a situation in which:
q.x: Jobless growth means output rises without matching growth in jobs.

q.s: The criterion with the highest weight in the 15th Finance Commission's formula for horizontal devolution was:
q.x: Income distance had 45%; population and area 15% each, demographic performance 12.5%, forest and ecology 10%, tax effort 2.5%.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a criterion in the 15th Finance Commission's formula for horizontal devolution?
q.x: The criteria were income distance, population, area, forest and ecology, demographic performance and tax effort.

q.s: The qualifications of the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission are laid down by:
q.x: The 1951 Act lays down the qualifications; the Chairman must have experience in public affairs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the 15th Finance Commission's grants to rural local bodies is correct?
o: Urban bodies must notify ceiling property-tax rates
The untied part may be used to pay salaries
60 per cent are tied grants and 40 per cent untied
q.x: Tied grants are for water and sanitation; untied grants cannot pay salaries; ULBs must notify floor rates.

q.s: 'Marble-cake federalism', with shared roles of the Union and the States, refers to:
q.x: Marble-cake federalism is cooperative federalism, NITI Aayog's guiding principle; layer-cake is dual federalism.

q.s: The Digital Payments Index (DPI), which measures the spread of digital payments in India, is compiled by the:
q.x: The RBI compiles and publishes the DPI semi-annually, since January 2021.

q.s: The Abid Hussain Committee (1997) dealt with:
q.x: Abid Hussain – SSI de-reservation; Rangarajan (1993) – disinvestment; Omkar Goswami – industrial sickness.

q.s: The Rangarajan Committee of 1993 was set up on the subject of:
q.x: The 1993 Rangarajan Committee dealt with disinvestment in public sector undertakings.

q.s: Under the SARFAESI Act, 2002, a borrower aggrieved by a lender's action under Section 13(4) may first appeal to the:
q.x: A Section 17 appeal lies to the DRT within 45 days; DRAT hears appeals from the DRT.

q.s: In the Union Budget 2026-27 'where the rupee goes', the single largest item was:
q.x: States' share of taxes (22%) was largest, followed by interest (20%).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a source of financing the fiscal deficit of the Union Government?
q.x: PSU dividends are non-tax revenue receipts; the deficit is financed by borrowings, small savings, provident funds and external loans.

q.s: During a recession, the government usually adopts which fiscal stance?
q.x: Expansionary policy (more spending, lower taxes) supports demand in a recession.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the FRBM Act, 2003 is correct?
o: It abolished the Budget's disclosure statements
It provides penalties for missing deficit targets
It applies directly to all States
It made fiscal discipline a legal duty of the Union Government
q.x: The Act has no penal provisions and binds only the Centre; States have their own FR laws.

q.s: The Debt Consolidation and Relief Facility, which encouraged States to enact Fiscal Responsibility laws, was recommended by the:
q.x: The Twelfth Finance Commission linked debt relief to State FR laws.

q.s: Which of the following is a direct tax?
q.x: STT falls on the investor who trades and is a direct tax; service tax was an indirect tax subsumed in GST.

q.s: Wealth tax, gift tax and estate duty were often called 'paper taxes' because they:
o: Were collected only on paper without payment
q.x: They yielded little revenue relative to the effort of collection.

q.s: Income tax was first introduced in India in 1860 by:
q.x: James Wilson, the first Finance Member, introduced income tax in 1860.

q.s: The 1997-98 Union Budget, called the 'dream budget', was presented by:
q.x: P. Chidambaram presented it, cutting income-tax rates to 10, 20 and 30%.

q.s: India's foreign exchange reserves first crossed US$ 100 billion in:
q.x: Reserves crossed $100 billion in December 2003; in January 1991 they had fallen to about $1.2 billion.

q.s: Which component forms the largest part of India's services trade surplus?
q.x: Software and IT-enabled services dominate the surplus, which financed about two-thirds of the merchandise deficit in FY25.

q.s: The cap on foreign investment in public-sector banks in India is:
q.x: Public-sector banks are capped at 20%; private-sector banks at 74%.

q.s: The 'Bharat Rice' brand, launched in February 2024 to provide rice to consumers at a subsidised price, is sold at:
q.x: Bharat Rice is sold at ₹29 a kg through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar.

q.s: The 'Blue Revolution' in India is associated with:
q.x: Blue – fisheries; Golden – horticulture and honey; Silver – eggs/poultry; Pink – meat, prawn and onion.

q.s: Which State leads India in the area under oil palm cultivation?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh leads with about 2.49 lakh ha, nearly half of India's oil palm area.

q.s: Under Annadata Sukhibhava – PM Kisan in Andhra Pradesh, a farmer family receives a total of how much per year?
q.x: ₹20,000 a year: ₹14,000 from the State and ₹6,000 from PM-KISAN.

q.s: The Agriculture Orientation Index for government expenditure (SDG indicator 2.a.1) is compiled by the:
q.x: The FAO compiles the Agriculture Orientation Index.

q.s: The Ashok Dalwai Committee was constituted to recommend measures for:
q.x: The Committee on Doubling Farmers' Income (base 2015-16, target 2022) submitted a 14-volume report and shifted focus from production to income.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Ashok Dalwai Committee is correct?
o: It recommended a shift from non-farm to farm jobs
It aimed to double farmers' nominal income
It aimed to double farmers' real income by 2022 with 2015-16 as base
It shifted the policy focus from income to production
q.x: The target was real income; it favoured a shift from farm to non-farm jobs and focus on income.

q.s: Which of the following agricultural research institutes is NOT located in or near Hyderabad?
o: National Academy of Agricultural Research Management
q.x: The Indian Institute of Maize Research is at Ludhiana.

q.s: The NABARD All India Rural Financial Inclusion Survey (NAFIS) 2021-22 is conducted by:
q.x: NAFIS is conducted by NABARD; AIDIS 2019 was part of the NSS 77th round.

q.s: The first national crop insurance scheme in India, the Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme, was introduced in:
q.x: CCIS began on 1 April 1985; NAIS replaced it in 1999-2000.

q.s: The Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme was first implemented in 2007 in which State?
q.x: WBCIS was first launched in Karnataka in Kharif 2007.

q.s: The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) was set up in 1995-96 within:
q.x: RIDF was created in NABARD with an initial corpus of ₹2,000 crore; irrigation takes the largest share.

q.s: Under the Price Support Scheme of PM-AASHA, procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is undertaken by:
q.x: Central nodal agencies NAFED and NCCF carry out PSS procurement.

q.s: NALCO, a Navratna CPSE headquartered at Bhubaneswar, functions under the:
q.x: NALCO is under the Ministry of Mines.

q.s: BHEL's Haridwar unit was established with the collaboration of:
q.x: Haridwar – USSR; Bhopal – Britain (AEI); Tiruchirappalli and Hyderabad – Czechoslovakia.

q.s: Under the New Public Sector Enterprise Policy for Atmanirbhar Bharat (2021), how many strategic sectors were identified?
q.x: Four broad strategic sectors were identified, each retaining a bare minimum of 1 to 4 CPSEs.

q.s: Which category accounts for the largest share of India's services exports?
q.x: Software and business services form the bulk (about 78%) of services exports, which far exceed services imports.

q.s: Which of the following changes was NOT introduced in the Union Budget 2017-18?
o: Advancing the budget date to 1 February
Merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget
q.x: The Outcome Budget dates from 2005; the other three were 2017-18 changes.

q.s: Part IXB of the Constitution dealing with cooperative societies was inserted by the:
q.x: The 97th Amendment (2011) inserted Part IXB; the Supreme Court later struck it down for State cooperatives, so it survives only for multi-State societies.

q.s: India is the world leader in which category of fisheries?
q.x: India leads in inland capture; most of the growth in fish production has come from inland aquaculture.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Buddhist site of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Srisailam is a Shaiva centre (Jyotirlinga); the others are Buddhist sites.

q.s: The MeeSeva citizen service delivery initiative of Andhra Pradesh was launched in:
q.x: MeeSeva was launched on 4 November 2011, growing out of eSeva (2001, under Chandrababu Naidu).

q.s: Which of the following statements about e-governance in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: eSeva (2001) was launched under N. Chandrababu Naidu
MeeSeva grew out of the APSWAN network
MeeSeva training was given through All India Radio
q.x: eSeva began in 2001 under Chandrababu Naidu; MeeSeva (2011) grew out of eSeva.

q.s: The Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS) is managed by:
q.x: SIDBI manages FFS, which invests through SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds, not directly.

q.s: The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant is located in which State?
q.x: Kudankulam is in Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Which of the following power projects is NOT a hydro-electric project?
q.x: Vindhyachal (Madhya Pradesh) is NTPC's largest thermal station.

q.s: The UDAY scheme launched in 2015 aimed at:
q.x: UDAY – DISCOM financial turnaround; Saubhagya – household electrification; DDUGJY – feeder separation.

q.s: Under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015, coal blocks are allocated by auction conducted by the:
q.x: The Nominated Authority under the Ministry of Coal runs the auctions.

q.s: When the RBI buys government securities through open market operations, bond yields tend to:
q.x: Purchases raise bond prices, and since prices and yields move inversely, yields fall.

q.s: On the Mohs scale of hardness, the mineral with a hardness of 8 is:
q.x: Topaz is 8; quartz 7, corundum 9, orthoclase 6.

q.s: Which of the following minerals is NOT harder than quartz on the Mohs scale?
q.x: Quartz is 7; orthoclase is 6, while topaz (8), corundum (9) and diamond (10) are harder.

q.s: In India, the main trigger of landslides and other mass movements is:
q.x: Monsoon rainfall is the main trigger, followed by earthquakes; the Himalaya and the North-East are most at risk.

q.s: Which of the following regions of India is NOT highly prone to landslides?
q.x: The Thar has gentle relief and low rainfall; the Himalaya, North-East and Western Ghats are landslide-prone.

q.s: The concept of the 'cycle of erosion' (1899), with stages of youth, maturity and old age, was put forward by:
q.x: Davis proposed the cycle of erosion; Penck held that uplift and erosion act simultaneously.

q.s: Which of the following statements about theories of landform development is correct?
o: W.M. Davis put forward his cycle of erosion in 1950
Walther Penck held that uplift and erosion act simultaneously
Davis held that landscape is a function of climate, vegetation and soil
In the Davisian cycle old age comes before maturity
q.x: Davis (1899) saw landscape as a function of structure, process and stage.

q.s: The Tigris and Euphrates join to form which waterway before entering the Persian Gulf?
q.x: Their confluence forms the Shatt al-Arab.

q.s: The river Amur, along the Russia–China border, drains into the:
q.x: The Amur flows north-east into the Sea of Okhotsk (Strait of Tartary).

q.s: Western disturbances are brought to north-west India in winter by the:
q.x: The Sub-Tropical Westerly Jet steers western disturbances; the Tropical Easterly Jet strengthens the SW monsoon.

q.s: The continental polar (cP) air mass originates over:
q.x: cP forms over the cold continental interiors of Siberia and Canada.

q.s: Which districts of Andhra Pradesh form the Scarce Rainfall agro-climatic zone?
q.x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone covers Kurnool and Anantapuramu.

q.s: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following States?
q.x: The Tropic passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram, not Odisha.

q.s: The Nokrek peak and biosphere reserve are located in which State?
q.x: Nokrek, the highest peak of the Garo Hills, is in Meghalaya; Kamet is in Uttarakhand.

q.s: The river known to the Greeks as 'Hydaspes', on whose banks Alexander fought Porus, is the present-day:
q.x: Hydaspes is the Jhelum; Acesines – Chenab, Hydraotes – Ravi, Hyphasis – Beas.

q.s: The largest tributary of the Godavari, formed by the Penganga, Wardha and Wainganga, is the:
q.x: The Pranhita joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram.

q.s: The Sabari, a tributary of the Godavari, is known in Odisha as the:
q.x: The Sabari is called the Kolab in Odisha and joins the Godavari near Kunavaram.

q.s: About 75 per cent of the area of Andhra Pradesh lies in the basins of the Godavari, Krishna and:
q.x: The Godavari, Krishna and Pennar basins together cover about three-fourths of AP.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, groundnut and castor are grown mainly on:
q.x: Groundnut and castor are mainly red-soil crops; chillies, turmeric and black gram do well on black soils.

q.s: Adoni and Aluru in Kurnool district are known for which type of soil?
q.x: Adoni and Aluru have deep black soils; Satyavedu and Puttur have elevated laterite.

q.s: According to the India State of Forest Report, 'Very Dense Forest' has a canopy density of:
q.x: VDF – 70% and above; MDF – 40-70%; Open Forest – 10-40%; Scrub – below 10%.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT counted as forest cover in the India State of Forest Report?
q.x: Scrub (canopy below 10%) is recorded separately and is not forest cover.

q.s: Flood forecasting in India is carried out by the:
q.x: The CWC under the Ministry of Jal Shakti runs flood forecasting.

q.s: Which of the following is a non-structural measure of flood control?
q.x: Flood-plain zoning and flood insurance are non-structural; embankments and dams are structural.

q.s: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre (ITEWC) is located at:
q.x: ITEWC is at INCOIS, Hyderabad, and can warn 25 Indian Ocean countries.

q.s: World Tsunami Awareness Day is observed every year on:
q.x: 5 November is World Tsunami Awareness Day.

q.s: The Barauni oil refinery is located in which State?
q.x: Barauni is in Bihar; Digboi (1901), India's oldest refinery, is in Assam.

q.s: Which of the following oil refineries is NOT located in Assam?
q.x: Barauni is in Bihar; Digboi, Guwahati, Bongaigaon and Numaligarh are in Assam.

q.s: Under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, the equity of Singareni Collieries Company Limited (SCCL) is shared between Telangana and the:
q.x: SCCL equity is 51% Telangana and 49% Government of India; AP has no share and must bring coal from farther away.

q.s: The Lower Sileru hydro-electric power house is located at:
q.x: Lower Sileru is at Mothugudem; the Narla Tata Rao thermal station is at Ibrahimpatnam.

q.s: The 'aman' rice crop of West Bengal is sown in June-July and harvested in:
q.x: Aman is the main kharif rice crop; aus is the autumn crop and boro the summer crop.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three rice crops of West Bengal?
q.x: Kuruvai is a short-term rice crop of Tamil Nadu.

q.s: The National Steel Policy 2017 targets a crude steel capacity of how many million tonnes by 2030-31?
q.x: NSP 2017, issued by the Ministry of Steel, targets 300 MT capacity.

q.s: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, Schedule A industries were:
o: Open to both the public and private sectors
q.x: Schedule A (17 industries) was State-reserved; Schedule B was open to both sectors.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Schedule A industry under the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956?
q.x: Machine tools were in Schedule B, open to both public and private sectors.

q.s: The first airport in India owned by a public limited company was:
q.x: Cochin International Airport (CIAL) was the first under public limited ownership.

q.s: Indian Airlines and Air India International were created under the:
q.x: The Air Corporations Act, 1953 nationalised the airlines into two corporations.

q.s: India's first deep-water transshipment port, Vizhinjam, is located in which State?
q.x: Vizhinjam is near Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala.

q.s: The largest private port of India is:
q.x: Mundra in Gujarat, run by Adani Ports, is the largest private port.

q.s: The Strait of Malacca separates the Malay Peninsula from:
q.x: The Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra; the Lombok Strait lies between Bali and Lombok.

q.s: Which of the following straits is NOT located in South-East Asia?
q.x: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman in West Asia.

q.s: India's largest import item by value is:
q.x: Crude petroleum is the largest import; petroleum products are also the top export.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's merchandise trade is correct?
o: Gold is India's largest import item
Petroleum products were India's top export item in 2024-25
India imports iron ore rather than exporting it
Gems and jewellery were India's top export in 2024-25
q.x: Petroleum products lead exports and crude oil leads imports; India exports iron ore.

q.s: The Lepakshi temple of Andhra Pradesh, on UNESCO's tentative list, was built under the:
q.x: The Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi (16th century) was built under Vijayanagara by Virupanna and Viranna.

q.s: The PRASHAD scheme of the Ministry of Tourism focuses on:
q.x: PRASHAD covers pilgrimage and heritage sites; Swadesh Darshan develops theme-based circuits.

q.s: According to the Census of India, a literate is a person aged ___ and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.
q.x: The Census counts persons aged 7 and above who can both read and write.

q.s: In the UNDP Human Development Report, a country with an HDI value of 0.800 and above is classified as:
The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is prepared by UNDP together with:
o: OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative)
q.x: The Global MPI is published by UNDP and OPHI.

q.s: According to NITI Aayog (January 2024), India's multidimensional poverty headcount fell from 29.17% in 2013-14 to about:
q.x: It fell to 11.28% in 2022-23.

q.s: Among the districts of Andhra Pradesh on the present 28-district map, the highest population density is found in:
q.x: Visakhapatnam has the highest density (about 1,870) and Polavaram the lowest (about 54).

q.s: As per Census 2011, the largest category of workers in Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Agricultural labourers, not cultivators, were the largest worker group in AP.

q.s: Which State of India has the largest number of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)?
q.x: Odisha has 13 PVTGs, the most of any State.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The Yerukula are a Scheduled Tribe but not a PVTG; Chenchu, Bondo Poroja and Kondareddi are PVTGs.

q.s: The headquarters of UN-Habitat is located at:
q.x: UN-Habitat is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya.

q.s: The concept of the 'Right to the City' (1968) was first given by:
q.x: Henri Lefebvre coined it; David Harvey developed it later.

q.s: The HRIDAY scheme of the Government of India covered how many heritage cities?
q.x: HRIDAY covered 12 heritage cities, including Amaravati in AP.

q.s: Which country was the world's largest recipient of remittances in 2024?
q.x: India received about USD 137 billion, the only country above USD 100 billion.

q.s: 'Ghotul' is the youth dormitory of which tribe?
q.x: Ghotul is the Gond (Muria) youth dormitory; the Oraon dormitory is Dhumkuria.

q.s: Among the matrilineal Khasi tribe, family property traditionally passes to the:
q.x: The youngest daughter (khadduh) inherits the ancestral property.

q.s: The High-Level Committee on the socio-economic status of tribal communities, set up in 2013, was headed by:
q.x: The Xaxa Committee reported in 2014; the Bhuria Commission (2002-04) was the second Article 339 commission.

q.s: The Ol Chiki script for the Santhali language was devised in 1925 by:
q.x: Pandit Raghunath Murmu devised Ol Chiki; Lako Bodra devised Warang Chiti for Ho.

q.s: India's first marine Biosphere Reserve (1989) is the:
q.x: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve was declared in 1989.

q.s: The northernmost coral reefs of India are found in the:
q.x: The Gulf of Kachchh reefs are the northernmost in India.

q.s: Which of the following conditions is favourable for the growth of coral reefs?
q.x: Corals need warm (above 20°C), shallow, clear, saline water; fresh or muddy water harms them.

q.s: The only Biosphere Reserve of Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: Seshachalam Hills is AP's biosphere reserve; NSTR is a tiger reserve.

q.s: Which tribal community serves as protection watchers in the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve?
q.x: The Chenchus, a PVTG of the Nallamala forests, work as protection watchers.

q.s: Cycas beddomei, an endemic 'living fossil' plant, is found in which protected area of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: SV National Park in the Seshachalam hills harbours Cycas beddomei, red sanders and the golden gecko.

q.s: 'Operation Brahma' (2025) was India's humanitarian relief mission after an earthquake in:
q.x: Operation Brahma was for the March 2025 Myanmar earthquake.

q.s: 'Operation Vanilla' (2020) by the Indian Navy was a relief mission to:
q.x: INS Airavat carried relief to Madagascar after Cyclone Diane.

q.s: The India Innovation Index, which ranks States on innovation, is published by:
q.x: NITI Aayog publishes the India Innovation Index; WIPO publishes the Global Innovation Index.

q.s: The Amaravati Quantum Valley in Andhra Pradesh is to host a Quantum System Two computer of which company?
q.x: IBM, with TCS and L&T, is installing its Quantum System Two at Amaravati.

q.s: India's first supercomputer, developed by C-DAC in 1991, was:
q.x: PARAM 8000 (1991) was the first; PARAM Padma (2003) was the first Indian entry on the TOP500 list.

q.s: The AI platform 'Krutrim' was developed by:
q.x: Krutrim is Ola's AI venture; OpenHathi is by Sarvam AI.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an Indian AI model or platform?
q.x: Cortana is Microsoft's virtual assistant.

q.s: India's first satellite placed in orbit by an Indian-made launch vehicle (SLV-3, 1980) was:
q.x: Rohini RS-1 (18 July 1980) made India the sixth nation to orbit a satellite on its own rocket; Aryabhata and Bhaskara used Soviet rockets.

q.s: Which of the following Indian satellites was NOT launched by a Soviet rocket?
q.x: Rohini RS-1 went up on India's own SLV-3 from Sriharikota.

q.s: India's first experimental Earth-observation satellite, launched in 1979, was:
q.x: Bhaskara I (1979) was India's first experimental remote-sensing satellite.

q.s: The SSLV-D1 mission of 2022 failed to place which satellites in the correct orbit?
q.x: SSLV-D1 put EOS-02 and AzaadiSAT into a wrong orbit.

q.s: The James Webb Space Telescope observes mainly in the:
q.x: JWST, a NASA-ESA-CSA mission launched in December 2021, is an infrared telescope.

q.s: India's first dedicated satellite for X-ray polarimetry is:
q.x: XPoSat (January 2024) made India the second country after the US (IXPE) with such a mission.

q.s: ISRO launched 72 OneWeb satellites in two missions using which launch vehicle?
q.x: Both OneWeb missions (2022 and 2023) used LVM3.

q.s: Which of the following is an example of active remote sensing?
q.x: Radar satellites like RISAT send their own signal; optical satellites like Resourcesat are passive.

q.s: India's solar mission Aditya-L1 is placed in a halo orbit around the Lagrange point L1, at a distance from the Earth of about:
q.x: L1 is about 1.5 million km from the Earth; Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57.

q.s: How many Lagrange points exist in a two-body system such as the Sun and the Earth?
q.x: There are five Lagrange points, L1 to L5.

q.s: 'Nuri' (KSLV-II), launched in June 2022, is the first indigenous launch vehicle of:
q.x: Nuri is South Korea's first indigenous rocket.

q.s: The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) on Aditya-L1 is designed to study the:
q.x: VELC studies the corona; SUIT images the photosphere and chromosphere; PAPA analyses solar-wind particles.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a payload of Aditya-L1?
q.x: CHACE was on the Moon Impact Probe of Chandrayaan-1.

q.s: In January 2022, which country became the first export customer of the BrahMos missile?
q.x: The Philippines signed a US$375 million deal for three shore-based BrahMos batteries.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India and nuclear regimes is correct?
o: India is a member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group
India follows export-control guidelines through the WMD Act and SCOMET list
India is a nuclear-weapon state under the NPT
q.x: India is outside the NSG, has not signed the CTBT or NPT, but follows export-control guidelines via the WMD Act and SCOMET.

q.s: The K9 Vajra-T self-propelled howitzer was developed under India's defence partnership with:
q.x: The K9 Vajra-T is built by L&T with South Korea's Hanwha.

q.s: The National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) functions under the:
q.x: NCIIPC, set up under Section 70A of the IT Act, is under NTRO.

q.s: Which of the following sectors is NOT covered by the NCIIPC as critical information infrastructure?
q.x: NCIIPC covers power, BFSI, telecom, transport, government and strategic sectors.

q.s: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act received Presidential assent on:
q.x: The DPDP Act got assent on 11 August 2023, after the earlier PDP Bill was withdrawn in 2022.

q.s: The Supreme Court declared the right to privacy a Fundamental Right in:
q.x: A nine-judge bench in Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy to be a Fundamental Right.

q.s: The Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam is being built and operated by:
q.x: PFBR was designed by IGCAR and is built and run by BHAVINI; it marks Stage II of India's nuclear programme.

q.s: In 1928, L.J. Stadler first induced mutations in barley using:
q.x: Stadler used X-rays; BARC Trombay has since developed 72 mutant crop varieties.

q.s: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) was set up in 2004 under the:
q.x: APTEL was set up under the Electricity Act, 2003 to hear appeals against regulators' orders.

q.s: The Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC) was set up under the:
q.x: APERC was set up under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998.

q.s: The Visakh refinery in Andhra Pradesh belongs to:
q.x: The Visakh refinery is HPCL's; the Kochi refinery is BPCL's.

q.s: Which of the following refineries does NOT belong to Indian Oil Corporation?
q.x: The Kochi refinery belongs to BPCL.

q.s: In wind energy, 'repowering' means:
o: Shifting turbines to new high-wind sites
Replacing ageing turbines with larger modern ones at the same site
Converting wind farms into solar parks
Adding battery storage to wind farms
q.x: Repowering replaces old turbines at the same site; the 2016 policy was replaced by the Repowering and Life Extension Policy, 2023.

q.s: Which of the following is a secondary air pollutant?
q.x: PAN and photochemical smog form in the air; CO, SO₂ and NO are emitted directly.

q.s: The concept of 'biodiversity hotspots' was proposed by:
q.x: Norman Myers proposed hotspots (1988); Dasmann coined 'biological diversity'.

q.s: To qualify as a biodiversity hotspot, a region must have at least how many endemic vascular plant species?
q.x: A hotspot needs at least 1,500 endemic vascular plants and must have lost at least 70% of its habitat.

q.s: In the classification of the components of the environment, microbes belong to the:
q.x: Microbes are biotic; nutrients, water and air are physical; political institutions are cultural.

q.s: The terms alpha, beta and gamma diversity were introduced by:
q.x: R.H. Whittaker introduced them; the Shannon-Wiener and Simpson indices measure species diversity.

q.s: Which of the following statements about measuring biodiversity is correct?
o: The Shannon-Wiener index measures ecosystem productivity
Species richness is the number of species and evenness their relative abundance
Species evenness is the number of species in an area
Gamma diversity is diversity within a single habitat
q.x: Shannon-Wiener and Simpson indices measure species diversity; gamma diversity is regional diversity.

q.s: India's first community-driven programme to remove invasive fish and restock native species was begun by BNHS at:
q.x: BNHS started it at Ujani reservoir; the banned African catfish is a threat at Keoladeo.

q.s: The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted in 2022 at:
q.x: It was adopted at CBD COP15 in Montreal; the Aichi Targets were adopted at COP10, Nagoya.

q.s: M-STrIPES, the patrolling and monitoring system used in Indian tiger reserves, was launched in 2010 by the NTCA and the:
q.x: NTCA and WII launched M-STrIPES; camera trapping and scat DNA replaced the pugmark method.

q.s: International Tiger Day is observed every year on:
q.x: International Tiger Day (29 July) was begun at the 2010 St Petersburg summit, which adopted TX2.

q.s: The headquarters of the Global Tiger Forum is located at:
q.x: The Global Tiger Forum is headquartered in New Delhi.

q.s: The second site for Project Cheetah in India, after Kuno National Park, is:
q.x: Gandhi Sagar WLS in Madhya Pradesh is the second site.

q.s: The Asiatic cheetah now survives in the wild only in:
q.x: A small population of Asiatic cheetahs survives only in Iran.

q.s: The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and adjoining areas replaced the:
q.x: CAQM, under the CAQM Act 2021, replaced the EPCA.

q.s: The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted in 1997 under the:
o: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
q.x: The CGWA was set up under Section 3(3) of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

q.s: Microplastics are plastic particles smaller than:
q.x: Microplastics are below 5 mm; nurdles are primary pellets of 1–5 mm.

q.s: The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) deals with:
q.x: UNCCD addresses desertification, land degradation and drought.

q.s: PFAS chemicals are commonly called:
q.x: PFAS persist in the environment for very long, hence 'forever chemicals'.

q.s: Flue Gas Desulphurisation (FGD) units in thermal power plants are installed to reduce emissions of:
q.x: FGD can remove up to 95% of SO₂ from flue gas.

q.s: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Flue Gas Desulphurisation removes carbon dioxide from flue gas
India's vehicle scrappage policy was introduced in 2021
All new vehicles in India must be E100-compatible
FGD for coal plants was first mandated in 2020
q.x: The scrappage policy came in 2021; FGD removes SO₂ and was mandated in 2015; vehicles are made E20-compatible.

q.s: The PRANA portal launched in 2021 is meant for monitoring the:
q.x: PRANA (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities) monitors NCAP.

q.s: 'Green mufflers' are used to reduce:
q.x: Green mufflers are 4-6 rows of dense trees along roads that absorb noise.

q.s: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, appeals against penalties imposed by the adjudicating officer under the Environment (Protection) Act lie to the:
q.x: Appeals lie to the NGT.

q.s: An appeal against an order of the National Green Tribunal lies to the:
q.x: Appeals lie to the Supreme Court within 90 days; the NGT is not bound by the CPC.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Green Tribunal is correct?
o: Only a serving Supreme Court judge can be its Chairperson
It is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
Appeals against its orders lie to the High Court
It is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure and follows natural justice
q.x: A retired SC judge or HC Chief Justice can head it; appeals lie to the Supreme Court.

q.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, Category A projects are granted environmental clearance by the:
o: MoEFCC after appraisal by the Expert Appraisal Committee
q.x: Category A projects are cleared at the Centre; Category B by the SEIAA.

q.s: The Montreal Protocol (1987) deals with:
o: Substances that deplete the ozone layer
q.x: The Montreal Protocol phases out ozone-depleting substances; the ozone layer is projected to recover to 1980 levels by about 2066 over Antarctica.

q.s: Which of the following statements about chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) is correct?
o: They are harmless to the ozone layer
They deplete the ozone layer and are also greenhouse gases
They were used mainly as fertilisers
They are produced naturally by volcanoes
q.x: CFCs deplete ozone, add to global warming and were used in refrigerators, ACs and aerosols.

q.s: Under India's PPV&FR Act, 2001, benefit sharing with farmers is through the:
q.x: Benefit sharing goes through the National Gene Fund; the Act bars registration of GURT varieties.

q.s: The International Solar Alliance was launched at COP21 (2015) by India and:
q.x: India and France launched the ISA at COP21 in Paris.

q.s: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched at the:
q.x: It was launched at the G20 New Delhi Summit in 2023; CDRI was launched in 2019 at New York.

q.s: 'Green GDP' is obtained by subtracting from GDP the:
o: Cost of natural resource depletion and environmental degradation
q.x: Green GDP = GDP minus net natural capital consumption.

q.s: In the Sustainable Development Report 2025, India entered the top 100 for the first time, with a rank of:
q.x: India ranked 99th of 167 countries in SDR 2025.

q.s: Griseofulvin is used in the treatment of:
q.x: Griseofulvin is an antifungal for ringworm; chloroquine is an antimalarial.

q.s: Nafithromycin, India's first indigenous macrolide antibiotic, is meant for treating:
q.x: Nafithromycin (Miqnaf) targets community-acquired pneumonia.

q.s: Atherosclerosis is a disease of the:
q.x: Atherosclerosis is plaque build-up in arteries, causing coronary artery disease.

q.s: The Aarogya Setu contact-tracing app was developed by the:
q.x: Aarogya Setu was developed by NIC under MeitY.

q.s: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is transmitted by the:
q.x: It is caused by Leishmania donovani and spread by female Phlebotomus sandflies.
